prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Miami for hurricane-rated roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there’s no single universal “best” — the right Miami contractor depends on your exact location, roof type, budget and whether they have proven HVHZ (high-velocity hurricane zone) experience and approvals. I can recommend companies if you want local names, but first I’ll give the fastest way to identify the best one for you.

What to require for a hurricane-rated roof replacement in Miami
- Miami‑Dade County / Florida approvals: materials and installation methods should meet Miami‑Dade County NOA (Notice of Acceptance) or be expressly rated for the HVHZ under the Florida Building Code.  
- Proper contractor licensing: a Florida certified roofing contractor license (verify the license number with the DBPR).  
- Insurance: contractor carries general liability ($1M+ recommended) and workers’ compensation (or an exemption). Ask for certificates naming you as additional insured while work is performed.  
- Manufacturer certification: prefer installers certified by major manufacturers (GAF/ELK, Owens Corning, CertainTeed, TAMKO, etc.). Manufacturer warranties matter only if installed by a certified installer.  
- Wind‑uplift engineering and proper attachments: hurricane straps/ties, ring‑shank nails, approved underlayment, oversized fasteners where required, sealed ridge and hip systems; contractor should provide uplift calculations if asked.  
- Permits and inspections: contractor pulls all required permits and arranges inspections.  
- Warranties and workmanship guarantee: get written factory and contractor warranties (length and transferability).  
- Local references and recent projects: ask for recent Miami/HVHZ jobs and contact references.

Questions to ask any candidate contractor
- Are you licensed in Florida? What’s your license number? (verify on the Florida DBPR site)
- Do you carry workers’ comp and general liability? Can you provide COIs?
- Have you done hurricane‑rated roof replacements in Miami‑Dade County? Can I see NOAs for the products you propose?
- Are you a certified installer for the shingle/metal product you recommend?
- Will you pull permits and coordinate inspections?
- What is included in the price (deck repairs, tear off, disposal, permit fees)?
- What warranties do you provide? Are they transferable?

Red flags
- No permit pull or refusal to write it in the contract.
- Contractor asks for large upfront cash payments (limit upfront to materials deposit).
- No proof of insurance or license, no references, or only out-of-area experience.
- Vague answers about Miami‑Dade approvals or manufacturer certification.

If you want, I can:
- Compile a short vetted list (3–5) of highly rated roofers in Miami if you give me your ZIP code or neighborhood. I’ll include why each is recommended and what to verify with them.
- Or draft an email/estimate checklist you can send to contractors.

Which would you prefer? Provide your ZIP or neighborhood and the roof type (asphalt shingle, tile, metal) and I’ll pull a tailored list of contractors and what to ask each.
